items.text: When your session has expired after a longer period of inactivity, a "Session expired" notice now appears instead of a 403 error. "Log in again" takes you back to the same page after signing in. Unsaved input is lost in the process.
The "Show remediated" switch in the vulnerability list now also shows CVEs that are no longer reported after the fix. These rows are greyed out and link to the detail page.
A subtle loading line below the header shows when data is loading after a filter or scope change.
The AI assistant (MCP server) can now fetch upgrade recommendations per component, list suppression rules, and follow or unfollow CVEs for you.
The "Newly discovered CVEs" chart now shows stacked bars per week instead of overlapping areas, which makes it easier to read.
The "What to fix first" overview is more compact. Components and fix versions are on the CVE detail page.

The AI assistant (MCP server) can now change the target date, notes and assignee of remediations and create remediations for several namespaces at once. Queries can also be narrowed to a cluster and namespace, filtered by vulnerability feed, and run without the global thresholds. Escalations are grouped as in the escalation view and returned page by page.
CVE descriptions no longer start with spaces or indented lines.
Comments on a CVE are now visible only to people who may also open the CVE detail page.
The upcoming escalations preview now shows no entries for a filter without matches, instead of entries outside your namespaces.
Risk acceptances imported from Excel for a single namespace are now approved automatically, like manually created ones. The import also works with access to all namespaces.
The management email saved in the settings is now used for the weekly digest and as escalation fallback.
PDF and Excel exports now apply every filter of the vulnerability list, for example remediation status, age and deployment.
After changes to priorities, risk acceptances, remediations and suppression rules, the vulnerability list and the dashboard refresh immediately.
The selected scope is kept when you open notifications or move between a CVE and a risk acceptance.

The AI assistant (MCP server) now filters risk acceptances by CVE correctly and returns risk acceptances and remediations page by page. Previously these inputs were ignored. Error messages now reach the assistant in English, and your email address is also stored when you first sign in through the assistant.
Open and in-progress remediations can now be edited: move or remove the target date, change the notes, unassign. A changed target date is recorded in the audit log.
The detail page of a fixed CVE stays reachable as long as you can see a remediation for it. You can keep commenting there.
Resolved remediations can now be reopened.
You now pick people everywhere in the same search dialog that is used for mentions.
The reason for "won't fix" no longer overwrites your notes and is shown separately.
Automatically resolved remediations are now labelled as such; your notes stay unchanged.

You can now get a daily summary email covering, among other things, overdue remediations, suppression rules, escalations, and expiring risk acceptances. It holds counts and links only. Turn it on per category in My settings; it is off by default.
The CVE alert summary can now also count new relevant CVEs of any severity. To use it, turn on the email for "New relevant CVEs" in My settings.

My settings is easier to read: the email for newly prioritized CVEs now sits in the "Prioritizations" row, and the two critical CVE switches are now one, "Alert email: critical CVEs". Your existing choices are kept. If you had turned on only one of the two switches, you now get both counts.
Each version now has a changelog. The changelog can be found in the sidebar.

New FAQ page under Help in the sidebar: it answers common questions about visibility, ratings, risk acceptances, remediations, escalations, notifications, and badges. The search is kept in the URL, so you can share a link to a filtered FAQ.
Hardened the validation of OIDC sign-in tokens.
Updated dependencies to fix known vulnerabilities.
Updated dependencies to fix known vulnerabilities.
Maintenance release with build fixes and no visible changes.

Subscribe to CVEs: use Subscribe on a CVE detail page to follow a CVE and get notified about comments, prioritization, risk acceptances, remediations, escalations, changed ratings, and new fixes. In the CVE list, the Subscribed only filter shows just your subscriptions.
Create remediations for several namespaces at once: tick one or more affected namespaces (or Select all) and one remediation is created per namespace.
Optional daily summary email in My settings: new critical CVEs, critical CVEs with a fix available, and newly prioritized CVEs. At most one email per day, with counts and links only.
Mentions in comments: typing @ opens a search dialog where you find users by name or username and pick them with the keyboard.
Hovering a point in the dashboard EPSS risk matrix now shows whether a fix is available in your scope.
The workflow steps on the CVE detail page now correctly show remediations in progress and requested risk acceptances.
The CVE detail page follows the cluster and namespace selected in the sidebar: deployments, components, and counts only cover that scope.
Fixed an issue in the Excel export.
Cross-cluster access: when your platform team groups clusters together, namespaces shared with you on a peer cluster also show up in the frontend of the other clusters in that group.
New My comments page: it lists every discussion you commented in, with your latest comment and how many replies arrived since.
Severity, CVSS, and EPSS are now the same in every view and scope. The rating of the most recently scanned image always wins.
